page: Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is a Cloud Compute virtual machine provisioned on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon processors. The instance provides 6 shared vCPUs derived from 3 physical cores with 2 threads per core operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2. Memory capacity is allocated at 16.0 GB, resulting in approximately 2.67 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include 320 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, with no dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark measurements indicate modest single-thread capabilities, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 823.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1272.09. Multi-threaded processing reaches average throughput levels in stress-ng at 6774.42, while Geekbench multi-core registers 3551.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 48.31 GB/sec, although write operations are more constrained at 18.72 GB/sec. Data processing tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression register in lower percentiles. In network-facing and caching tests, the instance achieves 6.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 5.39 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The shared CPU allocation model and moderate clock frequency make the vc2-6c-16gb an economical option for non-critical multi-threaded processes, balancing low cost per thread against reduced per-core execution speeds. The inclusion of 320 GB of fast local NVMe storage enhances its utility for workloads that require local file buffering without enterprise dedicated-core pricing. Primary workload fits include staging environments, continuous integration test runners, intermediate caching nodes, background worker pipelines, and light-to-moderate web serving.
description: Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is an entry-to-mid-tier Cloud Compute instance based on 6 shared Intel Xeon x86_64 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz across 3 physical cores. The instance is paired with 16.0 GB of system memory (2.67 GB per core), 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 1 public IPv4 address, with no GPU hardware. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate modest single-core throughput, balanced by moderate multi-core capabilities and solid in-memory transaction performance, achieving 6.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 48.31 GB/sec in large-block uncached read bandwidth. Due to its shared execution model and lower clock frequency, it exhibits lower efficiency in sustained compression and compute-intensive single-threaded tasks. The instance serves as a cost-effective platform for development servers, test automation, lightweight application hosting, background worker queues, and general-purpose non-latency-sensitive utilities.
